chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman, and after marrying her, he learned that she had committed fornication. He said: 'If her husband wishes, he may take the dowry from the one who married her off to him, and she is entitled to the dowry for having made her private part permissible to him; and if he wishes, he may leave her (keep her without divorce).'
ai.seo_question: What are the financial and marital consequences if a husband discovers his wife committed fornication after marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the husband's right of choice (*ikhtiyar*) upon discovering his wife's pre-marital fornication, a condition that affects the validity of the dowry distribution. The Imam specifies that the husband may claim the dowry back from the guardian (*wali*) who contracted the marriage, while the wife retains her share as compensation for consummation, or he may simply retain her without financial penalty. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that pre-marital zina does not automatically invalidate the marriage but grants the husband discretionary power regarding financial restitution.
